clarity-checker: Finds wording in a message, spec, or instruction that could materially change comprehension or execution, and proposes a minimal correction. Use when a user asks to check clarity, proofread for ambiguity, or verify that text will be understood the way it was intended before it is sent or published.
risk-scanner: Scans an artifact (message, plan, config, or code change) for risks that could make it unsafe, misleading, incorrect, or costly, and reports each risk with evidence and a minimal correction. Use when a user asks to check for risks, do a pre-send or pre-deploy safety pass, or find what could go wrong before acting.
evidence-checker: Separates demonstrated facts from assertions in a piece of text, classifying each claim as evidenced, inferred, unverified, or contradicted. Use when a user asks to fact-check a document, verify claims before relying on them, or tell evidence apart from speculation.
tone-fit-checker: Assesses whether the tone of a message fits its intended audience and purpose, and suggests up to three targeted corrections. Use when a user asks whether a message's tone is appropriate, wants to adjust tone for a specific audience, or is unsure if wording will land the wrong way.
root-cause-analyzer: Traces a problem from its observed symptom through immediate and deeper causes to a structural fix and prevention, marking hypotheses explicitly. Use when a user asks to find the root cause of an incident, bug, or recurring issue rather than just its workaround.
option-comparator: Compares a small set of realistic options against practical criteria (implementation speed, complexity, security, maintainability, cost, lock-in) and recommends the strongest option for the given context. Use when a user asks to compare approaches, tools, or designs before deciding which one to pursue.
requirement-quality-checker: Assesses whether a set of requirements is clear, testable, and implementation-ready, classifying each issue as a blocker, improvement, or acceptable. Use when a user asks to review requirements, a spec, or acceptance criteria before implementation starts.
edge-case-finder: Finds realistic edge conditions likely to break a requirement or implementation, prioritizing plausible business and system edges over exotic theoretical ones. Use when a user asks to find edge cases, stress-test a design, or check what inputs or conditions might break a feature.
